card.name: Verb after risk-group subject in warnings
card.fires_on: The word "are" right after a long list of patient risk groups, as in NSAID GI-bleeding warnings. Also weakly on "in" after "have been reported" and on a capitalised word piece in an all-caps patient heading.

modes.label: Are after risk factors
modes.description: "are" following a subject naming elderly patients or those with prior ulcer or bleeding history, before "at greater risk".
modes.example: Elderly patients and patients with a prior history of peptic ulcer disease and/or GI bleeding<< are>> at greater risk for serious GI events [

modes.label: In after reported
modes.description: "in" after "have been reported" before a percentage of patients.
modes.example: Notable elevations of ALT or AST (approximately three or more times the upper limit of normal) have been reported<< in>> approximately 1% of patients in clinical
